description: PR widens the eu-west-1a private subnet from a /24 to a /20 in terraform.tfvars. A subnet's cidr_block forces replacement, so the subnet is destroyed and recreated with a new id, and the two ledger nodes pinned to that AZ (subnet_id forces replacement) are destroyed and recreated with it. Acceptable: two new internal services (chargebacks, merchant-portal) allowed to reach the ledger on tcp 8443 from their own security groups (a security group rule widened inside the VPC). Noise: a CostCenter default tag on every resource, longer flow-log retention.

material.why: cidr_block 10.40.10.0/24 -> 10.40.16.0/20 forces replacement of the private subnet: everything in it must be destroyed first (here the two primary ledger nodes), the new subnet gets a new id, and anything outside this state that references the old subnet id (other stacks, Lambda/ENI configs, endpoint services) breaks.

subnet_id becomes unknown because its subnet is replaced, which forces replacement of the ledger node: the instance and its root volume are destroyed (outage of a primary shard, data on the root volume lost) and a new instance with a new private IP is launched.
Same as ledger-a1: replaced because the eu-west-1a private subnet it lives in is replaced; both primary ledger shards go down at once.
